correctness.rationale: For simple real spectrum, conjugating \(H^\dagger\eta=\eta H\) by the eigenvector matrix gives a positive diagonal \(D=V^\dagger\eta V\), hence \(\eta=V^{-\dagger}DV^{-1}\). The inverse metric and \(D^{-1/2}GD^{-1/2}\) have the same positive spectrum, proving the condition-number identity. Metric orthogonality of distinct eigenvectors gives the pairwise lower bound by comparing \(u_i\pm u_j\) to \(\lambda_{\min}\) and \(\lambda_{\max}\). In dimension two, AM-GM forces equal diagonal scaling and yields \((1+c)/(1-c)\), uniquely up to global scale. The bundled standard-library checker verifies representative instances but is not used as the infinite-quantifier proof.

value.rationale: The condition number is a natural scale-invariant measure of worst-case norm distortion, while metric nonuniqueness is a recognized structural issue in quasi-Hermitian quantum mechanics. Reducing the global finite-dimensional choice to diagonal Gram scaling gives a usable computational characterization, and the sharp pairwise obstruction quantifies unavoidable metric blow-up as eigendirections coalesce. The two-level formula is exact and model-independent rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
